back: Regulates new issues in the primary market: registration and prospectus. Often called the paper act or truth in securities act.
spoken: Securities Act of 1933. ... Regulates new issues in the primary market: registration and prospectus. Often called the paper act or truth in securities act.

back: Created the SEC. Regulates secondary-market trading, exchanges, broker-dealers, and insider trading.
spoken: Securities Exchange Act of 1934. ... Created the SEC. Regulates secondary-market trading, exchanges, broker-dealers, and insider trading.

back: Writes rules for municipal securities dealers and municipal advisors. Has no enforcement power: FINRA and the bank regulators enforce its rules.
spoken: MSRB. ... Writes rules for municipal securities dealers and municipal advisors. Has no enforcement power: FINRA and the bank regulators enforce its rules.

back: Up to $500,000 per separate customer capacity, including at most $250,000 in cash. Covers missing assets when a member firm fails, not market losses.
spoken: SIPC coverage (2026). ... Up to 500,000 dollars per separate customer capacity, including at most 250,000 dollars in cash. Covers missing assets when a member firm fails, not market losses.

back: Third market: exchange-listed securities traded over the counter. Fourth market: institutions trading directly with each other, without a broker-dealer.
spoken: Third market vs. fourth market. ... Third market: exchange-listed securities traded over the counter. Fourth market: institutions trading directly with each other, without a broker-dealer.

back: The FOMC buying or selling Treasuries. Buying adds money and pushes rates down. Selling drains money and pushes rates up.
spoken: Open market operations. ... The FOMC buying or selling Treasuries. Buying adds money and pushes rates down. Selling drains money and pushes rates up.

back: Move before the economy does: building permits, stock prices, new orders, initial jobless claims, average weekly hours.
spoken: Leading indicators. ... Move before the economy does: building permits, stock prices, new orders, initial jobless claims, average weekly hours.

back: The underwriter buys the entire issue as principal and bears the risk of any unsold shares.
spoken: Firm commitment underwriting. ... The underwriter buys the entire issue as principal and bears the risk of any unsold shares.

back: Net worth over $1 million excluding the primary residence. Or income over $200,000 single or $300,000 joint in each of the last 2 years. Holders of the Series 7, 65 or 82 also qualify.
spoken: Accredited investor (individual). ... Net worth over 1 million dollars excluding the primary residence. Or income over 200,000 dollars single or 300,000 dollars joint in each of the last 2 years. Holders of the Series 7, 65 or 82 also qualify.

back: At least 20 days after filing a registration statement. No sales. A red herring can be sent and indications of interest taken.
spoken: Cooling-off period. ... At least 20 days after filing a registration statement. No sales. A red herring can be sent and indications of interest taken.

back: It's unlawful to say the SEC approved a security or passed on its merits.
spoken: Section 23 of the 1933 Act. ... It's unlawful to say the SEC approved a security or passed on its merits.

back: Civil actions such as injunctions, fines, disgorgement and bars. Criminal cases are referred to the Department of Justice.
spoken: SEC enforcement powers. ... Civil actions such as injunctions, fines, disgorgement and bars. Criminal cases are referred to the Department of Justice.

back: The Federal Reserve Board, under Regulation T: 50% for stock purchases. FINRA sets maintenance requirements.
spoken: Who sets initial margin?. ... The Federal Reserve Board, under Regulation T: 50 percent for stock purchases. FINRA sets maintenance requirements.

back: FDIC insures bank deposits up to $250,000. SIPC restores missing securities and cash when a broker-dealer fails. Neither covers market losses.
spoken: FDIC vs. SIPC. ... FDIC insures bank deposits up to 250,000 dollars. SIPC restores missing securities and cash when a broker-dealer fails. Neither covers market losses.

back: Coverage is per capacity, such as individual, joint, IRA or trust. Two individual accounts in the same name share one limit.
spoken: SIPC separate capacity. ... Coverage is per capacity, such as individual, joint, IRA or trust. Two individual accounts in the same name share one limit.

back: Banks, insurers, registered investment companies, registered investment advisers, or any person with total assets of at least $50 million.
spoken: Institutional account (FINRA Rule 4512). ... Banks, insurers, registered investment companies, registered investment advisers, or any person with total assets of at least 50 million dollars.

back: Provides custody, clearing, margin financing, securities lending and consolidated reporting to large clients such as hedge funds.
spoken: Prime broker. ... Provides custody, clearing, margin financing, securities lending and consolidated reporting to large clients such as hedge funds.

back: Paid to give advice about securities. Owes clients a fiduciary duty. Regulated by the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.
spoken: Investment adviser. ... Paid to give advice about securities. Owes clients a fiduciary duty. Regulated by the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.

back: Advises municipal issuers on bond deals. Registers with the SEC and MSRB. Owes municipal entity clients a fiduciary duty.
spoken: Municipal advisor. ... Advises municipal issuers on bond deals. Registers with the SEC and MSRB. Owes municipal entity clients a fiduciary duty.

back: Transfer agent: keeps the shareholder list, issues and cancels certificates. Registrar: makes sure outstanding shares don't exceed authorized shares.
spoken: Transfer agent vs. registrar. ... Transfer agent: keeps the shareholder list, issues and cancels certificates. Registrar: makes sure outstanding shares don't exceed authorized shares.

back: Depository Trust Company, part of DTCC. Central depository that settles trades by book entry.
spoken: DTC. ... Depository Trust Company, part of DTCC. Central depository that settles trades by book entry.

back: Publicly offered corporate debt needs an indenture and an independent trustee acting for bondholders.
spoken: Trust Indenture Act of 1939. ... Publicly offered corporate debt needs an indenture and an independent trustee acting for bondholders.

back: Primary: the issuer sells new securities and gets the proceeds. Secondary: investors trade with each other.
spoken: Primary vs. secondary market. ... Primary: the issuer sells new securities and gets the proceeds. Secondary: investors trade with each other.

back: Exchange: auction market. OTC: negotiated dealer market. Most bonds trade OTC.
spoken: Exchange vs. OTC. ... Exchange: auction market. OTC: negotiated dealer market. Most bonds trade OTC.

back: An alternative trading system with no displayed pre-trade quotes. Used for large institutional blocks.
spoken: Dark pool. ... An alternative trading system with no displayed pre-trade quotes. Used for large institutional blocks.

back: Bid: the price a dealer pays, which is what a customer selling receives. Ask: the price a dealer sells at, which is what a customer buying pays. The difference is the spread.
spoken: Bid and ask. ... Bid: the price a dealer pays, which is what a customer selling receives. Ask: the price a dealer sells at, which is what a customer buying pays. The difference is the spread.

back: The NYSE firm responsible for a fair and orderly market in its assigned stocks. Formerly called the specialist.
spoken: Designated market maker. ... The NYSE firm responsible for a fair and orderly market in its assigned stocks. Formerly called the specialist.

front: Discount rate vs. fed funds rate
back: Discount rate: what the Fed charges banks. Fed funds: what banks charge each other overnight.
spoken: Discount rate vs. fed funds rate. ... Discount rate: what the Fed charges banks. Fed funds: what banks charge each other overnight.

back: What banks charge broker-dealers to finance customer margin loans. It's the basis for margin interest.
spoken: Broker call loan rate. ... What banks charge broker-dealers to finance customer margin loans. It's the basis for margin interest.

back: Selling securities, raising rates or raising reserve requirements. Rates rise and bond prices fall.
spoken: Fed tightening. ... Selling securities, raising rates or raising reserve requirements. Rates rise and bond prices fall.

back: The Federal Open Market Committee: the 7 Fed governors plus 5 Reserve Bank presidents. It directs open market operations.
spoken: FOMC. ... The Federal Open Market Committee: the 7 Fed governors plus 5 Reserve Bank presidents. It directs open market operations.

back: Short-term yields are above long-term yields. Often viewed as a recession warning.
spoken: Inverted yield curve. ... Short-term yields are above long-term yields. Often viewed as a recession warning.

back: Expansion, peak, contraction, trough.
spoken: Business cycle phases. ... Expansion, peak, contraction, trough.

back: Two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP. The NBER makes the official call using broader measures.
spoken: Recession rule of thumb. ... Two consecutive quarters of declining real GDP. The NBER makes the official call using broader measures.

back: High inflation combined with high unemployment and slow growth.
spoken: Stagflation. ... High inflation combined with high unemployment and slow growth.

back: Current assets minus current liabilities. A measure of short-term liquidity.
spoken: Working capital. ... Current assets minus current liabilities. A measure of short-term liquidity.

back: Keynesian: use fiscal policy to manage demand. Monetarist: control the money supply.
spoken: Keynesian vs. monetarist. ... Keynesian: use fiscal policy to manage demand. Monetarist: control the money supply.

back: GDP: output within a country's borders. GNP: output by a country's residents and companies, wherever it's produced.
spoken: GDP vs. GNP. ... GDP: output within a country's borders. GNP: output by a country's residents and companies, wherever it's produced.

back: Trade in goods and services, plus income and transfers. Part of the balance of payments.
spoken: Current account. ... Trade in goods and services, plus income and transfers. Part of the balance of payments.

back: Helps U.S. exporters and U.S. holders of foreign assets. Hurts importers and Americans traveling abroad.
spoken: Weak dollar effects. ... Helps U.S. exporters and U.S. holders of foreign assets. Hurts importers and Americans traveling abroad.

back: Manager's fee is the smallest. Underwriting fee is next. Selling concession is the largest.
spoken: Underwriting spread components. ... Manager's fee is the smallest. Underwriting fee is next. Selling concession is the largest.

back: Syndicate members commit capital and share liability. Selling group members act as agents with no liability.
spoken: Syndicate vs. selling group. ... Syndicate members commit capital and share liability. Selling group members act as agents with no liability.

back: Allowed under Regulation M at or below the public offering price, and must be disclosed in the prospectus.
spoken: Stabilizing bid. ... Allowed under Regulation M at or below the public offering price, and must be disclosed in the prospectus.

back: Disclosure document for a municipal bond issue. Delivered by settlement under MSRB Rule G-32.
spoken: Official statement. ... Disclosure document for a municipal bond issue. Delivered by settlement under MSRB Rule G-32.

back: 506(b): no general solicitation, up to 35 non-accredited investors. 506(c): general solicitation allowed, but all buyers must be verified accredited investors.
spoken: Rule 506(b) vs. 506(c). ... 506(b): no general solicitation, up to 35 non-accredited investors. 506(c): general solicitation allowed, but all buyers must be verified accredited investors.

back: 6 months for reporting issuers, 1 year for non-reporting issuers. File Form 144 if selling more than 5,000 shares or more than $50,000 in 90 days.
spoken: Rule 144 holding period. ... 6 months for reporting issuers, 1 year for non-reporting issuers. File Form 144 if selling more than 5,000 shares or more than 50,000 dollars in 90 days.

back: Resales of restricted securities to qualified institutional buyers, generally those with at least $100 million in securities.
spoken: Rule 144A. ... Resales of restricted securities to qualified institutional buyers, generally those with at least 100 million dollars in securities.

back: 25 days for exchange-listed IPOs. 90 days for unlisted IPOs. 40 days for unlisted follow-on offerings.
spoken: Aftermarket prospectus delivery. ... 25 days for exchange-listed IPOs. 90 days for unlisted IPOs. 40 days for unlisted follow-on offerings.
